resources.string: Shapes the TLS handshake toward the edge so DPI has a harder time matching it. Off by default; each mode changes the bytes on the wire.
Split and decoy modes only apply to the HTTP/2 carrier. Turn on "MASQUE over HTTP/2" on the Connection page to use them; on HTTP/3 the ClientHello sits inside QUIC frames the engine does not split.
Spoofing shapes a TLS ClientHello, which WireGuard and WARP×2 do not send. Pick a MASQUE transport on the Connection page to use it.

Experimental: sends a harmless prefix record before the real ClientHello. Whether it helps depends on the network, and it can also break a strict middlebox. Certificate pinning stays on, so a fake answer still cannot open the tunnel - the connection either validates end to end or fails.

Presented to the MASQUE edge instead of the default name. The edge certificate is pinned, so a wrong name cannot open you to interception - but the edge may also refuse it. Leave empty for the default. Applies from the next connect.
